questions.q: What is the programme mainly about?
options: How social media helps people talk
World records for long phone calls
What makes a good conversation
How to become a radio presenter
questions.why: Neil says 'we're talking about talking' and they discuss Nihal Arthanayake's book on better conversations.

questions.q: Why do some people think the art of conversation is being lost?
options: Social media makes us talk without listening
People are too busy to meet their friends
Phone calls have become too expensive
Schools no longer teach it to children
questions.why: Sam says Twitter and social media encourage us to give opinions without always listening in return.

questions.q: What did Nihal learn from his mother, a nurse?
options: That talking a lot makes you popular
That you should avoid strangers
That work is more important than talking
That listening to others enriches you
questions.why: He says it gave him the sense that you are enriched by listening.

questions.q: Why was conversation also a 'survival instinct' for Nihal?
options: He was often in danger at home with his family
He was a brown boy in a mostly white school
He had to work in a shop from a young age
He was very shy and had few friends
questions.why: He says he was a little brown boy in a predominantly white state school in the 1980s.

questions.q: What happens when we 'listen to reply', according to Nihal?
options: We understand the other person better
We ask more questions
We think more about what we'll say next
We stop talking completely
questions.why: Neil says we think about the next thing we want to say more than understanding the other person.

questions.q: Which of these does Nihal say conversation is NOT?
options: A way to build bridges
An art form
Something that has changed history
Two politicians talking over each other
questions.why: He says it's not tittle-tattle, shouting on social media, or two politicians talking over each other.

questions.q: What does good conversation involve, according to Sam?
options: Taking turns rather than talking over people
Speaking louder than the other person
Talking mainly about yourself
Keeping it very short
questions.why: She says it involves taking turns, not talking over someone.

questions.q: How does Sam describe her meeting with her old school friend?
options: They argued a lot about politics
They listened, and hours flew by
They talked only about other people
It was short and rather awkward
questions.why: She says they both listened, and before they knew it a couple of hours had passed.
